## Historical audit — S0136

**Scope:** Only chunk 1 of 2 is visible. All citations below refer to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C2/selection/commons_138420790/trajectory.jsonl`. The reference and rendered images themselves are not visible in this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 | The explicit goal was a separate-mesh Blender reconstruction of a 384 × 512 indoor photograph, matching viewpoint, framing, occlusion and materials. The student’s interpretation was a kitchen; that semantic identification is not independently verified here (student response, line 3). |
| Student response and execution, lines 3–5 | The first program constructed multiple assemblies: architecture, two columns, island, hood, cabinetry and oven tower, plus smaller fixtures. It included solid panels, separate drawer faces and a grouped island; the sink was represented by layered boxes rather than a cut opening. Code configured procedural wood grain, roughness, camera, world and lights. These are operations, not proof of visual fidelity or physical connections. Step 1 returned `ok: true` and saved a render and scene. |
| Student revision, lines 7–12 | The runner supplied the step-1 result and render for comparison. The student estimated that the post was too far left and the island end too narrow, hypothesized camera azimuth as the cause, changed camera position and target, moved the hood, and regrouped the faucet while copying its materials. Step 2 executed successfully and was selected. The diagnosis and expected image movement are student estimates, not independent measurements. |
| Student revision, lines 13–18 | After step-2 feedback, the student reported a pale wall occluding much of the view and attributed it to the left wall crossing sightlines. The executed step 3 moved that wall and foreground post, expanded architecture, and retained the camera. The runner reported `ok: true`, saved the render and scene, and recorded selection of step 3. Whether the wall diagnosis or correction was visually correct is unverified. |

**Teacher input and exploration:** No distinct teacher message, teacher detection, diagnosis or proposed update appears in this visible chunk; consequently there is no evidence of teacher receipt or adoption. The student did receive runner instructions and actual render feedback, and made two self-directed revisions in response. The recorded CLI sessions report zero tool calls, with external Blender executions performed by the runner (lines 2, 4–5, 8, 10–11, 14, 16–17).

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Three builds and renders succeeded technically, and step 3 was selected in the visible record. Final task outcome and formal visual correctness remain **unknown**: selection and successful rendering do not establish accurate geometry, pose, lighting, textures, part attachment or reference match. The student specifically flagged uncertain hood attachment and room proportions; the later wall-occlusion hypothesis cannot be checked without the images. No conclusion is drawn about the unseen chunk.

**Lessons:** Transferably, an executable render enables a subsequent, testable distinction between camera and local occlusion hypotheses, but a successful execution alone validates neither. The particular post, hood and wall adjustments are task-specific; their effectiveness remains unresolved.
